title: lcnet
text:
The exported checkpoints are inference graphs. RepDWConv has already been fused into one depthwise convolution, and batch-norm on the backbone is folded into the convolution bias. The recognition neck keeps its own batch-norm, which is why BatchNorm lives next to the backbone that no longer uses it.
from fastcore.test import test_eq

test_eq(_unit_stride(1), True)
test_eq(_unit_stride((1, 1)), True)
test_eq(_unit_stride((2, 1)), False)
_unit_stride((2, 1))

False
A residual is legal only when the stride is 1 in both directions and the channel count does not change. The recognizer’s (2, 1) blocks are not residuals.

title: lcnet
text:
Batch-norm


source

BatchNorm
def BatchNorm(
    channels:int, eps:float
)->None:
Inference batch-norm. Running statistics are weights.


This is inference batch-norm: the running statistics are weights, not buffers that update. LightSVTR uses it. The backbone does not, because those batch-norms were folded into the convolution bias before export.

Squeeze-excite


source

SqueezeExcite
def SqueezeExcite(
    channels:int, alpha:float, *, reduction:int=4, residual:bool=False

Global pool, 1x1 bottleneck, hardsigmoid. Optional residual adds the gated map.

title: lcnet
lcnet
text:
Stem


source

DetStem
def DetStem(
    mid:int, out:int
)->None:
Multi-branch stem. Total stride is 4.


The stem’s total stride is 4: one stride-2 convolution, then a stride-2 convolution after the branches merge. The 2×2 branch is padded (0, 1, 0, 1), which is the asymmetric SAME the exporter used. The other branch is a 2×2 max pool with the same asymmetry. Both recognizer and detector use this stem.

title: weights
text:
Parameter order follows the module tree, which is the order the Paddle exporter emitted Conv, ConvTranspose, BatchNormalization, MatMul, and the decomposed LayerNorm scale and bias. Paddle linear weights are stored as (in, out). MAX linear weights are (out, in).
A bias is the next Add, skipping Identity nodes, whose right-hand side is a learned vector. A scalar add is not a bias. LayerNorm scale is the same kind of vector sitting on a Mul, and the bias is the Add that follows it.


source

arrays_from_graph
def arrays_from_graph(
    graph:Graph
)->list[np.ndarray]:
Learned tensors in module state-dict order.


Conv weights stay in the checkpoint’s layout. conv2d was built with permute=True so that layout is already OIHW. MatMul is the exception: the stored matrix is (in, out) and MAX wants (out, in), so it is transposed here.

import numpy as np
from fastcore.test import test_eq
from solid_lens.onnx import Graph, Node

weight = np.arange(6, dtype=np.float32).reshape(2, 3)
graph = Graph()
graph.initializers["w"] = weight
graph.initializers["b"] = np.array([10, 20, 30], np.float32)
matmul = Node()
matmul.op_type = "MatMul"
matmul.name = "fc"
matmul.inputs = ["x", "w"]
add = Node()
add.op_type = "Add"
add.inputs = ["y", "b"]
graph.nodes = [matmul, add]
arrays = arrays_from_graph(graph)
test_eq(arrays[0].tolist(), weight.T.tolist())
test_eq(arrays[1].tolist(), [10.0, 20.0, 30.0])
arrays[0]

array([[0., 3.],
       [1., 4.],
       [2., 5.]], dtype=float32)




source

checkpoint_arrays
def checkpoint_arrays(
    path:Path
)->list[np.ndarray]:
Learned tensors in an ONNX checkpoint, in module state-dict order.


MAX walks layer_weights and then sublayers. Defining a submodule later in __init__ puts its tensors later. That is the same order as the exporter, which is why the layer notebooks keep the attribute order they do.


source

load_checkpoint
def load_checkpoint(
    module, path:Path
)->None:


A count mismatch and a shape mismatch are both errors. There is no partial load. If a new layer is inserted in the wrong place, this is the function that says so.

title: RepLKPAN
text:
The checkpoint is the reparameterized inference graph. Each dilated large-kernel branch is one depthwise 9×9 plus a pointwise mix, and the IntraCL batch-norm is folded into the closing 1×1. Submodules are stored in the order the exporter wrote them. Changing that order will not fail at construction. It fails when a checkpoint tensor has the wrong shape.
source

LargeKernel
def LargeKernel(
    in_channels:int, out_channels:int, kernel:int
)->None:
Depthwise convolution followed by a pointwise mix.

title: RepLKPAN
text:
IntraCL


source

IntraCL
def IntraCL(
    channels:int, reduce_factor:int=2
)->None:
Strip and square context at 7, 5, and 3, added back onto the input.


At each scale the square kernel and the two strips (vertical, then horizontal) are added, then the next smaller scale reads that sum. The projection is a residual on the block input. Attribute order is the checkpoint order, including the 7-then-5-then-3 groups.

title: RepLKPAN
text:
The neck


source

RepLKPAN
def RepLKPAN(
    in_channels:tuple[int, int, int, int], out_channels:int, kernel:int
)->None:
Top-down fusion, a bottom-up path, then IntraCL. Four levels are concatenated at the finest resolution.


Top-down first: the coarsest lateral is upsampled onto the next finer map. Then a bottom-up path downsamples the fine mix back onto the coarse ones. IntraCL runs on each level, and the four maps are concatenated at the finest resolution. The output width is fpn_channels, because each level was projected to fpn_channels // 4.

title: ocr
text: Pages are resized and boxes are read off the detector map the same way as PaddleOCR: keep the aspect ratio, then take DB contours, a minimum-area rectangle, and an unclip. Recognition is CTC over the LightSVTR sequence. Compilation stays inside main, so the geometry below can be read on its own.

title: ocr
text:
Detector size
These are the PP-OCRv6 medium overrides from PaddleOCR’s OCR pipeline. The checkpoint yaml is looser (0.2 / 0.45 / 1.4). The pipeline that produces the boxes uses the numbers below.


source

detection_hw
def detection_hw(
    height:int, # Page height, in pixels
    width:int, # Page width, in pixels
    limit_side_len:int=64, # Side the limit type compares against
    limit_type:str='min', # `min`, `max`, or `resize_long`
    max_side_limit:int=4000
)->tuple[int, int]:
Detector height and width. Same rule as PaddleOCR DetResizeForTest type 0.


limit_type is min and limit_side_len is 64, so a page whose short side is already at least 64 is not shrunk. Both sides are then rounded to a multiple of 32, and nothing is allowed below 32. round is bankers’ rounding, so a half step lands on the even multiple.

from fastcore.test import test_eq

test_eq(detection_hw(100, 200), (96, 192))
test_eq(detection_hw(40, 80), (64, 128))
test_eq(detection_hw(100, 400, limit_side_len=64, limit_type="resize_long"), (32, 64))
detection_hw(100, 200)

(96, 192)

Class 0 is the blank. Repeated labels collapse, and blanks separate the repeats that should survive.

test_eq(_ctc_decode([1, 1], ["a"]), "a")

title: ocr
text:
Boxes
The unclip distance is the DB post-process offset: area times the ratio, divided by the perimeter. Round joins match PaddleOCR.


source

boxes_from_bitmap
def boxes_from_bitmap(
    prob:np.ndarray, dest_width:int, dest_height:int, *, thresh:float=0.3, box_thresh:float=0.6,
    unclip_ratio:float=1.5, max_candidates:int=3000
)->list[tuple[int, int, int, int, float]]:
PaddleOCR DBPostProcess quads, returned as axis-aligned boxes.


Coordinates come back in the original image. The recognizer crops that rectangle. Boxes are sorted top to bottom, then left to right. A contour whose short side is under 3 pixels, or whose mean score is under 0.6, is dropped. After the unclip the short side must clear 5.

import numpy as np
from fastcore.test import test_eq

prob = np.zeros((64, 64), np.float32)
prob[20:36, 8:48] = 0.95
boxes = boxes_from_bitmap(prob, 64, 64)
test_eq(len(boxes), 1)
left, top, right, bottom, score = boxes[0]
test_eq(score > 0.6, True)
test_eq(left < 8, True)
test_eq(right > 48, True)

title: onnx
text: The official checkpoints are ONNX. Loading them does not require the onnx package or a runtime. A graph is a protobuf message: nodes in exporter order, initializers, and the input and output shapes. weights walks that node list.

title: onnx
text:
Varints
Protobuf integers are base-128, little-endian, with the high bit set on every byte but the last.

title: onnx
text:
Messages
One message is a sequence of (field_number, wire_type, payload). Wire 0 is a varint, 1 is 8 bytes, 2 is a length-delimited blob, and 5 is 4 bytes.


source

fields
def fields(
    buf:bytes
)->list[tuple[int, int, bytes | int]]:
Return (field_number, wire_type, payload) for one message.


150 is the protobuf specimen for a varint: the bytes 96 01. Field 1, wire 0, is the key byte 08 in front of that. Zigzag maps even numbers to non-negative integers and odd numbers to negative ones.

from fastcore.test import test_eq

test_eq(_varint(bytes([0x96, 0x01]), 0), (150, 2))
test_eq(fields(bytes([0x08, 0x96, 0x01])), [(1, 0, 150)])
test_eq([_zigzag(v) for v in range(4)], [0, -1, 1, -2])
fields(bytes([0x08, 0x96, 0x01]))

[(1, 0, 150)]

handwriting
text:
The page is a lined hearing note in print, not cursive: a date, who was in the room, a direct-examination outline, and an objection. The file is nbs/samples/hwr.png. Margin labels, arrows, and the tier diagram are on the page.
The reference is those words, including the margin labels. Arrow strokes are not words, so they are left out. A line the model invents still counts against the error rate.

The scan
The file is nbs/samples/hwr.png. Cells from here on compile graphs, so a plain nbdev-test skips them.

title: handwriting
text:
Read the page
One detector graph for this shape, then the shared 48×320 recognizer. The note is letterboxed, with its aspect kept, onto the 1056×1792 detector already compiled, so this cell opens that cache instead of building a new graph. The times after that are a warmup plus the median of five reads. Detection is one forward pass. Recognition is the sum of the line crops.

import time

from solid_lens.model import compile_detector, compile_recognizer
import numpy as np

from solid_lens.ocr import (
    detection_hw,
    detect_boxes,
    load_charset,
    load_image,
    recognize_crop,
    resize_hwc,
)

def letterbox(image, out_h, out_w):
    "Scale to fit, then pad with white. The detector shape stays a multiple of 32."
    height, width = image.shape[:2]
    scale = min(out_w / width, out_h / height)
    fitted_h = max(1, int(round(height * scale)))
    fitted_w = max(1, int(round(width * scale)))
    fitted = resize_hwc(image, fitted_h, fitted_w)
    canvas = np.full((out_h, out_w, 3), 255, np.uint8)
    top = (out_h - fitted_h) // 2
    left = (out_w - fitted_w) // 2
    canvas[top:top + fitted_h, left:left + fitted_w] = fitted
    return canvas

image = letterbox(load_image(PAGE), 1792, 1056)
height, width = image.shape[:2]
det_h, det_w = detection_hw(height, width)
charset = load_charset(ROOT / "models" / "ppocrv6_dict.txt", add_space=True)

t0 = time.perf_counter()
detector = compile_detector(
    height=det_h,
    width=det_w,
    cache_dir=ROOT / "models" / f"native_medium_det_{det_h}x{det_w}.mef",
)
detector_ready = time.perf_counter() - t0
t0 = time.perf_counter()
recognizer = compile_recognizer(cache_dir=ROOT / "models" / "native_medium_rec_48x320.mef")
recognizer_ready = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f"page {width}×{height} px, detector {det_w}×{det_h}")
print(f"detector ready in {detector_ready:.2f}s, recognizer ready in {recognizer_ready:.2f}s")

def read_timed(image):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    boxes = detect_boxes(image, detector)
    detect_s = time.perf_counter() - t0
    lines = []
    recognize_s = 0.0
    for left, top, right, bottom, score in boxes:
        t1 = time.perf_counter()
        text = recognize_crop(recognizer, image[top:bottom, left:right], charset)
        recognize_s += time.perf_counter() - t1
        if text:
            lines.append((text, score, left, top, right, bottom))
    return lines, detect_s, recognize_s

read_timed(image)
runs = [read_timed(image) for _ in range(5)]
lines, detect_s, recognize_s = min(runs, key=lambda run: run[1] + run[2])
detect_ms = sorted(run[1] for run in runs)[len(runs) // 2] * 1000
recognize_ms = sorted(run[2] for run in runs)[len(runs) // 2] * 1000
page_ms = sorted(run[1] + run[2] for run in runs)[len(runs) // 2] * 1000
print(f"{len(lines)} lines")
print(f"median detect {detect_ms:.0f} ms, recognize {recognize_ms:.0f} ms, page {page_ms:.0f} ms")

detector ready in 0.77s, recognizer ready in 0.31s
54 lines
median detect 4312 ms, recognize 3103 ms, page 7588 ms

title: handwriting
text:
Accuracy and speed
Character error rate is the Levenshtein distance divided by the length of the reference, after casefolding and dropping punctuation. A line the model adds makes that rate worse. Character recall is the longest common subsequence divided by the reference length, so it says how much of the note was recovered even when extra text was read.

from IPython.display import Markdown

hypothesis = " ".join(text for text, *_ in lines)
metrics = score_text(hypothesis, REFERENCE)
summary = f"""
| | |
|---|---:|
| lines | {len(lines)} |
| reference characters | {metrics['characters']:.0f} |
| reference words | {metrics['words']:.0f} |
| character error rate | {metrics['cer']:.1%} |
| character recall | {metrics['character_recall']:.1%} |
| character precision | {metrics['character_precision']:.1%} |
| word error rate | {metrics['wer']:.1%} |
| detector, median | {detect_ms:.0f} ms |
| recognizer, median | {recognize_ms:.0f} ms |
| page, median | {page_ms:.0f} ms |
| detector graph ready | {detector_ready:.2f} s |
| recognizer graph ready | {recognizer_ready:.2f} s |
"""
display(Markdown(summary))
print(hypothesis)

title: config
text: Detection uses PPLCNetV4, a RepLKPAN neck with IntraCL, and the inference DB head. Recognition uses the same backbone with height-only downsampling, then a LightSVTR neck and a CTC head. The NRTR head exists only while training, so it is not in these graphs.

title: config
text:
Blocks
A block is (kernel, in_channels, out_channels, stride, use_se). Stride is a pair when the recognizer downsamples height and keeps the width.
Detection stages s1 to s4 are the four maps the neck reads. Total stride at the end of the stem plus s1 is 4, then each later stage halves both sides.
Recognition never strides in width inside the backbone. Height is reduced twice, by the (2, 1) blocks, and the rest of the way by the pool in front of the neck.

from fastcore.test import test_eq

test_eq(DET_BLOCKS["s1"][0], (3, 128, 128, 1, True))
test_eq(REC_BLOCKS["b4"][0][3], (2, 1))
test_eq(len(REC_BLOCKS["b4"]), 7)
REC_BLOCKS["b5"][-1]

(3, 768, 768, 1, False)

def RecognizerConfig(
    stem_mid:int=64, stem_out:int=128, backbone_channels:int=768, svtr_dim:int=192, svtr_depth:int=2,
    svtr_heads:int=8, mlp_ratio:float=4.0, local_kernel:int=7, num_classes:int=18710, image_height:int=48,
    image_width:int=320, se_alpha:float=0.16666666666666666, bn_eps:float=1e-05, final_norm_eps:float=1e-06
)->None:
Backbone width, SVTR size, and the 48×320 image for the medium recognizer.


The CTC head has 18710 classes: the PP-OCRv6 dictionary, plus the blank. The recognizer’s image is 48×320. Two global transformer blocks run at width 192. The norm after the last block is tighter than the norms inside the blocks, 1e-6 rather than 1e-5.

from fastcore.test import test_eq

rec = RecognizerConfig()
test_eq((rec.image_height, rec.image_width), (48, 320))
test_eq(rec.svtr_dim % rec.svtr_heads, 0)
test_eq(rec.num_classes, 18710)

Device
The reference graphs are float32 on CPU. A compiled cache can be reloaded without rebuilding the graph.

title: solid_lens
text: Detection is PPLCNetV4, a RepLKPAN neck, and the inference DB head. Recognition uses the same backbone with height-only downsampling, a LightSVTR neck, and CTC. The official ONNX checkpoints supply the weights. The notebooks in nbs/ are the source; nbdev-export writes this package.

title: solid_lens
text:
Install
The graph runtime is Modular MAX, installed here with pixi. Checkpoints are local and are not part of the package.
pixi install
pixi run download

title: solid_lens
text:
Read a page
read_page returns each line as text, detector confidence, and an axis-aligned box in the original image.

from pathlib import Path
from solid_lens.core import repo_root
from solid_lens.model import compile_detector, compile_recognizer
from solid_lens.ocr import detection_hw, load_charset, load_image, read_page

root = repo_root()
image = load_image(Path("page.png"))
det_h, det_w = detection_hw(*image.shape[:2])
detector = compile_detector(
    height=det_h, width=det_w,
    cache_dir=root/"models"/f"native_medium_det_{det_h}x{det_w}.mef")
recognizer = compile_recognizer(cache_dir=root/"models"/"native_medium_rec_48x320.mef")
charset = load_charset(root/"models"/"ppocrv6_dict.txt", add_space=True)
read_page(image, detector, recognizer, charset)

The same pipeline is a command, and a JSON service on port 5001:
pixi run ocr page.png
pixi run serve
POST one or more files to /ocr as images or image. Each result has the file name and a list of fragments: text, norm, score, and box.

title: solid_lens
text:
Develop
Edit the notebooks. The modules under solid_lens/ are generated, and each one names the notebook to change.
nbdev-export
nbdev-test
nbdev-test runs the lessons that do not need MAX. nbdev-test --flags notest also executes the cells that build graphs, which needs the pixi environment.
The reading order follows a forward pass. config is the architecture. onnx reads a checkpoint. The layer notebooks are the blocks max.nn does not ship. detector and recognizer stack them, weights binds the checkpoint, model compiles, and ocr is the page pipeline.

title: download
text:
requirements.txt is a manifest, not a pip file. Each line is a filename and a URL. The files land in models/ at the checkout root.
Blank lines and comments are skipped. A line that is not two tokens is an error, which is what we want from a hand-edited manifest.

from fastcore.test import test_eq

names = [name for name, _ in _entries()]
test_eq(names, ["medium_det.onnx", "medium_rec.onnx", "ppocrv6_dict.txt"])

title: conv
text: max.nn.Conv2d(permute=True) keeps filters in OIHW order, which is how Paddle exported them. A stride-2 kernel-2 transposed convolution does not compile in this MAX build (num_groups fails to infer). With the kernel equal to the stride and no padding, the four taps do not overlap, so the transpose is four pointwise mixes interleaved on the spatial axes.

title: conv
LightSVTR
text:
The exported graph is the inference network. Dropout is gone. Each Conv-BN-Swish stays unfused, and each LayerNorm is a learned scale and bias. Two global transformer blocks sit between a 1×7 depthwise conv and an additive 1×1 skip. The NRTR decoder is not in the checkpoint.
source

LayerNorm
def LayerNorm(
    channels:int, eps:float
)->None:
Scale and bias. The checkpoint stores them as a Mul followed by an Add.
The checkpoint does not contain a LayerNorm op. It contains the scale and the bias, and weights finds those as a Mul followed by an Add. This module is the pair those tensors belong to.
source

ConvBNSwish
def ConvBNSwish(
    in_channels:int, out_channels:int, eps:float
)->None:
1x1 projection used by the skip and the channel reduction.
source

LocalMixer
def LocalMixer(
    channels:int, kernel:int, eps:float
)->None:
1xk depthwise conv along the text width, added back onto its input.
The local mixer is a 1×7 depthwise conv along the sequence, then batch-norm and SiLU, added back to its input. It does not mix height. By the time it runs, the map is one row tall.

title: LightSVTR
text:
Attention


source

SVTRBlock
def SVTRBlock(
    dim:int, num_heads:int, mlp_ratio:float, eps:float
)->None:
Pre-norm global attention and a Swish MLP. Dropout is identity here.


The scale multiplies the query only. That is how the exported graph is written, and it is not the same op as scaling the scores after the matmul when the dtype is not exact. The MLP is SiLU, not GELU. Dropout is absent, so it is not in the module.


source

LightSVTR
def LightSVTR(
    in_channels:int, dim:int, depth:int, num_heads:int, mlp_ratio:float, local_kernel:int, eps:float,
    final_eps:float
)->None:
Local conv, global blocks, then an additive skip of the backbone features.


The skip is constructed first because the exporter emits it first. final_eps is 1e-6 and applies only to the norm after the last block. The blocks themselves use eps, which is 1e-5.

title: server
text: The process holds one recognizer, compiled once, and a detector per input size. The detector graph is fixed-shape, so a new page size compiles a new graph and then reuses it. GET / describes the contract. POST /ocr accepts multipart files in images or image.

title: DB head
text:
Two stride-2 transposed convolutions restore the input resolution. The probability map is a sigmoid over one channel.
coordinate_transform_mode=2 and round_mode=2 are the MAX names for the nearest-neighbor mode the exported graph uses. RepLKPAN calls this with factors 2, 4, and 8.


source

DBHead
def DBHead(
    in_channels:int, hidden:int
)->None:
Two stride-2 transposes. The probability map is a sigmoid over one channel.


The 3×3 reduces the fused neck to 64 channels. Each transpose doubles the spatial size. The second one emits the single-channel probability map.

title: recognizer
text:
LCNetV4, then a height pool, the LightSVTR neck, and a CTC head. The backbone strides in height only. The pool finishes that reduction so the neck sees a single row.


source

PPOCRV6Recognizer
def PPOCRV6Recognizer(
    config:RecognizerConfig | None=None
)->None:
LCNetV4, a height pool, LightSVTR, and a CTC head.


Softmax is over the class axis. CTC decoding in ocr reads the argmax, so the probabilities are what the checkpoint’s inference graph emits.


source

avg_pool_height
def avg_pool_height(
    x:TensorValue
)->TensorValue:
3x2 average pool. Recognition features are one row tall afterwards.


The squeeze and unsqueeze put a singleton height back. LightSVTR still wants NCHW, and it removes that height itself when it builds the sequence.

title: model
text:
The detector is one graph per input shape, because both sides are fixed and must be multiples of 32. The recognizer is one graph, 48×320. A cache directory of compiled MEFs is reused; an empty directory is where a new compilation is written.
A non-empty cache is loaded. An empty one receives the compiled model. The directory is the cache key the callers choose, including the detector’s height and width in the name.
